claim_en: אפיך ("your nostrils") is written FULL with a yod exactly twice: בזעת אפיך ("in the sweat of your nostrils," Gen 3:19) and ברוח אפיך ("by the breath of Your nostrils" the waters piled up, Exod 15:8) — the Masorah's own mnemonic: man's livelihood is as hard as the splitting of the Sea of Reeds.

וילבשם ("and He clothed them") appears twice in the Masorah (the received spelling tradition): here and Lev 8:13 (Moses clothes Aaron's sons in tunics) — teaching that the Holy One made PRIESTLY garments for the first man; Bereshit Rabbah adds the firstborn served in them.
The garments verse has exactly EIGHT words — corresponding to the eight garments of the priesthood.

עקב ("heel") in this pointing stands three times in the Masorah's list: the serpent's heel-strike (3:15), Gad's blessing והוא יגד עקב ("he shall raid at the heel," Gen 49:19 — the Kitzur folds the serpent-likened tribes into one blessing), and Ps 41:10 (outside the Torah DB). Torah-side: exactly the two.

לשמר ("to guard") read as a notarikon (initial-letter cipher): its four letters open לילין שדין מזיקין רוחין ("night-beings, demons, harmers, spirits") — the guarded way warded against them. SNAPSHOT locks the cipher's base letters.
זאת ("this") in the serpent's indictment carries a dagesh (doubling dot) in the zayin — the doubling that binds it to עשית ("you did") before it.
עצבונך ("your toil") — the tsadi carries a dagesh (doubling dot).

כי עפר אתה ("for dust you are") — אתה ("you") carries zaqef qatan ("small upright," a pause accent) and is stressed on its FIRST syllable; the Great Masorah's list of first-syllable-stressed אתה opens HERE: the mortality verse heads the list.

ודרדר ("and thistles") — both dalets pointed with patach (the flat a-vowel); some copies point the second with qamatz, and Minchat Shai rules patach with all his books — SNAPSHOT sides with the ruling.
בזעת ("in the sweat") — the precise codices read mahpach ("inverted horn" accent) on the ayin; SNAPSHOT's chain reads exactly that.

כי שמעת ("because you listened") — "must be with ONE zarqa only, on the tav": the zarqa (= zinor, "pipe" accent) the unit's own parse flagged as the rare near-poetic register marker over both sentence-openers, attested from outside.

ויאמר ("and He said") opening the serpent's sentence carries telisha qetana ("small detached" accent; Minchat Shai's term tarsa) — "one sign only, on the resh": the postpositive sign sits once, on the word's last letter.
ויעש ("and He made") of the garments verse likewise carries telisha qetana ("small detached" accent) — "one tarsa alone."

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 3:17 (Ben Asher vs Ben Naftali)
claim_en: תאכלנה ("you shall eat of it") — Ben Naftali reads the kaf with plain sheva; Ben Asher, "on whom we rely," with chataf patach (the hurried a-vowel) — SNAPSHOT reads chataf patach: the letter follows Ben Asher.

"In the Torah of Rabbi Meir they found written כתנות אור — garments of LIGHT" (aleph for ayin): the tradition's own record of a manuscript variant. The received letter and SNAPSHOT read עור ("skin") with ayin — the frozen unit's letter-variant detector tripwire, now read at its source.

Minchat Shai reads galgal ("wheel," the day-old-moon accent) on אלהים ("God") and on כי ("because" — "with galgal, not maqqef," the joining hyphen) where SNAPSHOT's chain reads mercha / munach (both conjunctive accents) — manuscript accent-variant class, same class as gen_10's revia gap.
